negative_anchor.interpretation: Reusing activation loads across four rows and two projections increased register pressure and instruction count enough to erase CQ3's bandwidth advantage. The standard row kernel remains the correct optimization target.

hypothesis: The generated AVX2 loop serializes all 40 scaled block contributions through one YMM floating-point accumulator. CQ3 has two independently scaled 128-weight groups per 256-weight block. Accumulating group 0 and group 1 through separate YMM dependency chains and combining them once at the end should overlap FMA latency without changing packing, decoded ternary digits, integer dot products, scales, or storage.

implementation.base: Pinned llama.cpp plus CQ3 v1 and the rejected x86 pair-kernel test harness
implementation.single_independent_change: Replace the single CQ3 FP accumulator with one compile-time group-0 chain and one compile-time group-1 chain in ggml_vec_dot_cq3_0_cq8_0.
unchanged: all integer digit decoding and dot-product operations
all per-group FP16 and activation scales

stop_rules: Stop before timing if any CQ3 correctness test fails.
Reject before model integration if the exact Qwen3.8-27B MLP shape improves by less than 8% or is unstable.
Run the exact 20-item CUTE diagnostic even after a performance rejection, but do not let it override the performance decision.
Do not change storage, scales, weights, or evaluation data in this experiment.
claim_boundary: A pass would establish a faster exact-shape 2.125-bit CQ3 AVX2 primitive and justify selective 27B integration. It would not establish a whole-model ternary speedup, broad quality, final-node throughput, energy gains, 100 accepted tok/s, novelty, or a breakthrough.
